newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Offshore and local exporter dollar selling spurred the rand to a five-cent intraday gain on Monday before local demand and profit-taking forced it to relinquish some gains in the afternoon session.
At 1410 GMT, the rand was pegged at 4.4365/4395 against the dollar from 4.4825/4855 on Friday, after touching a day's strongest level of 4.4270 bid against the dollar shortly before 1000 GMT.

In the morning session, the currency hurried to around the 4.4250 level amid some talk of Reserve Bank assistance, although dealers felt the move was triggered by offshore selling which caught the local market long of dollars.

"What market players did after Stals two Tuesday's in a row was hope to take stop losses out (at the 4.50 level) so they were very long," a trader said, referring to Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals' comments that the speed of the rand's recent appreciation may have been a slight overadjustment.
"With Reserve Bank intervention (the longs) had to liquidate," the dealer added.
A large U.S investment bank operating out of London was believed to have been an active seller around the 4.47 level, one trader said. "They dumped a load," he said.
Another dealer said exporters had also entered the fray, using the opportunity to sell their dollars after last week's attempt at the psychological 4.50 level failed.
By noon, the currency had stabilised around the 4.43 level.
Dealers said the currency's steadying in the afternoon was due to profit-taking and local demand at the lower levels as the market became slightly cautious of being long dollars.
"The market is now being very wary of being long," one trader said noting that the speed of the move earlier had caught some players by surprise.
Dealers said the currency was expected to test lower levels again on Tuesday.
Against the crosses, the rand was last quoted at 7.2333/2426 against sterling from 7.2442/2567 on Friday and at 0.3762/3767 marks from 0.3758/3764 previously.
Activity on the bond market was lethargic in part because the market was jittery ahead of Thursday's economic indicators, dealers said.
January trade data is scheduled for release from Tuesday, while GDP, consumer inflation, money supply and private sector credit extension data is due on Thursday.

Little foreign interest was seen in the local bond market, dealers said, possibly due to the need for clearer signals from the money market -- where traders said short-term rates were too high for further long bond gains in the short-term.
"Bonds are very nervous. It's on a very tight band and until the money market eases and the indicators are released I do not expect a breakout," one trader said.

"There's also a lot of profit-taking by investment banks in London. We're seeing institutional buying and foreigners taking profits. Between 68 and 58 -- that's where we'll be trading for the first half of the week," he added.
At 1410 GMT the benchmark R150 was at 14.64 percent from 14.66 pct on Friday.
On the money market, rates held steady between 16.50 and 16.70 percent, while the 90-day BA rate was also unmoved at between 15.90 and 16.10 percent.
The Reserve Bank quoted the shortage at 10.286 billion rand on Saturday from 10.291 billion rand on Friday.
Bond Exchange statistics show foreigners sold 56.58 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Friday after selling 270.98 million rand's worth on Thursday.
Nominal cumulative volume on Friday was 3.2 billion rand from 43.43 billion rand on Thursday which is settlement day.
-- Juliette Saunders, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482-1003
